record.final_answer:
Short answer: the one setting that actually bounds the damage is the stream's `max_buffered_messages`. Thistlewire 0.9 has no built-in flow control for server-streaming, and the default is `0`, meaning unlimited — the server will queue ticks for a stalled dashboard until the process dies. Set it to a finite cap; when the cap is hit Thistlewire closes that stream with `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` rather than growing.

Two caveats on that, then the rest:

- I could not re-verify the docs: `thistlewire.example/docs/streaming` (and the host root) now return 404. The details above come from a July 2026 read of the 0.9 streaming docs. Your pin is 0.9.4, same minor line, so it very likely still holds — but confirm the option name and semantics against the 0.9.4 package before you write code.
- A cap only protects you if writes are actually attempted. A half-open TCP connection from flaky Wi-Fi never drains and never trips the cap, so its queue pins memory forever. Whatever keepalive / write-timeout options 0.9.4 exposes, set them — that's what evicts the zombie. I don't know those option names, so don't take a name from me here.

Sizing the cap

It's in messages, not bytes, so two numbers drive it: ticks/sec per dashboard and seconds of stall you're willing to absorb. Cap ≈ rate × tolerable_lag, times some headroom. At 200 symbols × 10 ticks/s that's 2,000 msg/s, so 5s of tolerance ≈ 10k. The real constraint is RAM per stalled client × how many clients you'll tolerate being stalled at once — do that multiplication before picking the number.

Better lever, if you can afford it: don't queue ticks, conflate them. Prices are latest-value data, so a slow client doesn't need the intervening ticks — keep one slot per symbol and overwrite. That makes per-client memory a function of symbol count, which is fixed and tiny, instead of a function of stall duration. You can then use a large cap purely as a "this client is effectively dead, drop it" tripwire rather than a memory bound. Coalescing into small batches also cuts per-message overhead and makes the message-count cap mean something predictable.

Adjacent things worth configuring while you're in there

- Cap concurrent streams per client. The buffer cap is per stream; one machine opening 50 streams multiplies your budget by 50. If Thistlewire 0.9 doesn't expose a per-client stream limit, enforce it in your handler.
- Keep the write off the feed loop. If the shared upstream feed blocks pushing into any single stream, one sluggish dashboard becomes a stall for every dashboard. Hand off to a per-stream bounded queue and let the writer drain it.
- Design the client contract around disconnects now, not later. `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` means the dashboard must reconnect and resubscribe, and it will have missed ticks. Give it a snapshot-then-stream path (or re-sync from the existing unary `prices.Get`) so recovery is correct rather than silently gappy.

Then verify with a deliberately slow reader: one client that reads a few messages then stalls, watch RSS plateau instead of climbing, and confirm the stream gets closed at the cap.
